plos-pone-0003444: Immunologists watched evolution happen inside patients in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003544: Cancer researchers isolated the roots of a deadly thyroid tumor in this 2008 paper. Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is among the most aggressive cancers, and the team identified CD133-positive cancer stem-like cells driving it in the lab. plos-pone-0003644: In 2008, a team studied faulty calcium control in weak muscle. plos-pone-0003744: In 2008, Wimberly, Hildreth, and Boyte asked why West Nile lingers on the northern plains. Mapping the 2003 epidemic's ecological niche, they found the landscape and climate factors keeping risk high there. The niche map explains a regional hotspot of a national disease.
plos-pone-0003844: In 2008, Shaw, Lindholm, and Prajsnar discovered a new stress chief in staph bacteria. Sigma S, a novel component of Staphylococcus aureus stress and virulence control, was identified and characterized. The finding adds a master switch to the portrait of a formidable pathogen.
plos-pone-0003944: In 2008, Habuchi, Tsutsui, and Kochaniak introduced mKikGR, a single-chain light switch. The monomeric photoswitchable fluorescent protein can be toggled on and off for imaging. The compact tool expands the palette for tracking molecules in living cells.
plos-pone-0004044: In 2008, Adrian Melott found a slow pulse in the history of life. Fossil data showed marine biodiversity rising and falling on a 63-million-year cycle. plos-pone-0004144: In 2009, Lu, Lin, and Kuo linked diabetes to faster aging. Their review tied diabetes to cognitive, mobility, and mood decline. The pooled studies covered many aging signs. Diabetes emerged as a whole-body aging driver. The pattern urges earlier screening in diabetic patients.
plos-pone-0004244: In 2009, Fernandez, Fu, and Pascual measured Spain's smoke-free law. The Spanish smoking ban cut second-hand smoke exposure in hospitality venues. plos-pone-0004344: In 2009, Kenny, Ward, and Josefsson found staph surviving human skin's natural oil. Staphylococcus aureus countered unsaturated long-chain free fatty acids well. The germ's survival tricks and virulence shifts were mapped fully. The neat finding exposes a chink in staph's armor.
plos-pone-0358644: Ringing ears and low mood travel together — but do the questionnaires measuring them ask the same questions twice? plos-pone-0358444: In the lava fields of northwest Saudi Arabia stand mustatils — mysterious Neolithic stone structures. plos-pone-0358044: Telling ‘la’ from ‘ra’ — or ‘ba’ from ‘ga’ — is genuinely hard for young ears. plos-pone-0356544: Breakthrough infections and imperfect vaccines don’t just fail individuals — they drive pathogen evolution. plos-pone-0352744: Classifying desert rangeland plants from drones — with only a handful of examples — is brutally hard. plos-pone-0355844: The African sugarcane stalk borer — Eldana saccharina — tunnels through profits across Tanzania. plos-pone-0355044: Educational professionals need reliable ways to assess theory of mind-related skills in children with autism. This paper designed, developed, and pilot-tested exactly such a scale. plos-pone-0357044: Henan Province’s vegetation has shifted dramatically since 2000. This paper monitored those changes through 2023 and analyzed the driving factors behind them. The two-decade trends give land managers the evidence to protect what’s greening — and restore what’s browning.
plos-pone-0356244: Computer-aided detection could find more tuberculosis cases in Ghana — but is it worth the money? plos-pone-0342144: Weight-based mistreatment at work — fat shaming on the job — is finally being studied. This exploratory study investigated the correlates of experiencing it. The findings name a form of workplace discrimination that has hidden in plain sight.

plos-pone-0353944: Female volleyball players with dynamic knee valgus — knees collapsing inward on landing — face high ACL tear risk. plos-pone-0355744: HIV patients with persistent low-level viremia face a dilemma: switch regimens or stay the course? plos-pone-0356144: Leishmania parasites smuggle molecular messages into human immune cells via exosomes. plos-pone-0345444: Urban infrastructure supply chains snap under stress — unless predictive analytics sees the break coming. plos-pone-0336744: Elderly South Koreans from rural regions flock to Seoul’s hospitals — a concentration the pandemic tested. plos-pone-0355544: Female university students faced the pandemic with fear — and coped in varied ways. This paper examined fear and coping strategies, testing physical activity and infection status as moderators. The findings show what buffered young women’s mental health when the world shut down.
plos-pone-0355944: Tracking Legionella — the pneumonia-causing bacterium — in the environment needs fast, accessible genomics. plos-pone-0354744: Eye health systems need complete profiles — beyond prevalence numbers. europmc-pmc2816644: Tumors starved of oxygen turn on a characteristic set of genes, and this 2010 paper distills it. europmc-pmc2846344: Leptin is famous for signaling fullness, but it also talks to the immune system. This 2010 review examines the role of leptin in activating immune cells. europmc-pmc2860244: A companion study widens the Oct4 web further. europmc-pmc2901944: Wound infections after surgery cost more than the hospital stay. This 2003 paper measures the health and money toll of surgical site infections found after patients go home. europmc-pmc2907344: Cancer drugs that save lives can wound hearts. This 2010 review pools randomized trials to weigh heart harm from anthracycline drugs, a mainstay of chemo. The authors pin down how often the damage strikes and who is at risk. Their numbers guide safer chemo choices for patients.
europmc-pmc2913244: Cells marching together need to touch to stay oriented. This 2010 paper shows group movement toward signals needs contact-based cell polarity. The authors reveal the touching rule behind group migration. Their work matters for wound healing and cancer spread alike.

europmc-pmc2993644: Unnecessary C-sections harm mothers, this 2010 WHO survey finds. The authors link surgery without medical need to worse short-term outcomes for mothers across countries. europmc-pmc3056144: Protein models need their hydrogens placed. This 2009 paper brings Protonate3D, a tool that adds missing hydrogens to protein models. europmc-pmc3069744: Diffraction data got an auto toolbox. This 2011 paper covers the autoPROC pipeline for processing crystal data. The authors' automation sped crystallography. europmc-pmc3087144: Preeclampsia shadows newborns too. This 2011 paper tracks how mothers' preeclampsia shapes babies' health. The authors reveal the newborn risks. Their work guides delivery care. europmc-pmc6514244: Standard DNA sequencing reads short fragments, which struggles with big rearrangements - the large insertions, deletions, and repeats behind many genetic disorders. europmc-pmc6710244: Period-tracking apps quietly amassed one of the largest reproductive datasets ever - over 600,000 cycles. pmc-13461544: A 2026 study of nurse-led bladder training's effect on urinary tract outcomes after kidney transplantation. The nursing intervention worked. The effect informs transplant care.
pmc-13467544: This 2026 paper evaluated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activity of a Cannabis sativa-infused African product used for wound healing. The traditional remedy was tested. The evaluation is the ethnopharmacology.
pmc-13421544: A 2026 prospective study validating an automated AI-based system for detecting age-related macular degeneration in clinical settings. The AI's eye disease detection was validated. The validating is the clinical evidence.
arxiv-2606-16144: Money thinkers now lean on AI and code, yet share few proof-checked tools. EconCSLib is a free code chest for money math, penned in Lean — a checker that vets each proof line. It hands money pros and AI folk a base they can trust.
arxiv-2606-16244: AI coding assistants sometimes write code with security holes. SPARK tackles that two ways: "security knowledge priming" feeds the model security know-how up front, and representation-guided activation steers it toward safe patterns as it writes. The paper presents the approach for researchers building code-generating AI that doesn't introduce vulnerabilities.
arxiv-2606-16444: At a rare 'hand-point' of some sky-math rules, the tug-bit gains a weird log twin that fades slow. This paper trails the twirl-flow and that log twin at the hand-point, charting how they bend the rules. Deep sky-math for tug-theory dreamers who chase odd gravity.
arxiv-2606-16544: Light beats in glass threads and chill-gas waves heed one wave-rule (Schrödinger lines); wed N such lines and waves wed too. This math paper names every rest shape of the N-wed set and proves none wobble. For wave-rule pros. Full lists, firm proofs.
arxiv-2606-16744: Two systems are 'bisimilar' if they behave the same from the outside — a key idea in checking software. This paper studies how hard bisimilarity and model checking are for finitary diagrams: how the cost grows. It is a theoretical computer science result for verification researchers.
